sources: NTA press release on NEET (UG) 2026 results, 16 July 2026 — https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s37bc1ec1d9c3426357e69acd5bf320061/uploads/2026/07/20260716477215762.pdf
exams.overview:
NEET (UG), the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for undergraduate courses, is the single entrance exam for medical and dental education in India. Under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019 and the laws governing dentistry, Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy, admission to MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BSMS, BUMS and BHMS courses in every medical institution in the country goes through NEET. That includes AIIMS and JIPMER, which have used NEET since 2020. Indian citizens and OCI cardholders who want to study medicine abroad must also qualify it.

The National Testing Agency has conducted NEET since 2019. Its role is limited to running the exam, declaring results and passing All India Ranks to the counselling authorities. The syllabus is set by the National Medical Commission, and seats are allotted afterwards through counselling: the Medical Counselling Committee for the 15% All India Quota and central institutions, and state authorities for state quota seats.

The exam is one paper, taken with pen on an OMR sheet in a single shift. It has 180 compulsory multiple-choice questions in three hours: 45 in Physics, 45 in Chemistry and 90 in Biology, split across Botany and Zoology, for 720 marks. A correct answer earns 4 marks and a wrong one loses 1. Because Biology is half the paper, a strong Biology score matters as much as Physics and Chemistry combined. The paper is offered in 13 languages, from English and Hindi to Tamil, Telugu and Urdu.

To sit NEET you must be at least 17 by 31 December of the exam year; there is no upper age limit. You need Class 12 or an equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Biotechnology and English, including practicals. Students waiting for their Class 12 results can take the exam but must have passed by the first round of counselling.

Qualifying NEET is measured in percentiles of the highest score: the 50th percentile for General and EWS candidates, and the 40th for SC, ST and OBC candidates, with separate thresholds for candidates with disabilities. Qualifying makes you eligible for counselling; your All India Rank decides which seat you can get. Ties are broken by Biology marks first, then Chemistry, then Physics.

The scale is very large. In the 2026 cycle close to 20 lakh candidates sat the exam at 5,440 centres in 551 Indian cities and 14 cities abroad, and 11.21 lakh qualified. The exam first held on 3 May 2026 was followed by a re-examination on 21 June 2026, and NTA declared results on 16 July 2026. Only 1,492 candidates scored 650 or more out of 720, which shows how sharply the competition narrows near the top.

The best preparation follows the official syllabus unit by unit: 20 units each in Physics and Chemistry and 10 in Biology. Practise full papers under exam timing, because three hours for 180 questions leaves one minute per question. Use the pattern and syllabus pages here to plan, and always confirm dates and rules on neet.nta.nic.in before you act on them.

exams.overview:
CUET (UG), the Common University Entrance Test for undergraduate admissions, is how students get into bachelor’s programmes at India’s Central Universities and at the many State, Deemed and private universities that have chosen to use it. Instead of sitting a separate entrance test for each university, a student takes one set of tests and sends the score to every participating university they apply to. NTA describes it as a common platform meant to give students from rural and remote areas the same opportunity as everyone else.

The National Testing Agency conducts CUET (UG). Its job ends at registration, running the tests, answer keys, results and the score card. Each university makes its own merit list from CUET scores and runs its own admissions, so questions about seats, cut-offs and counselling go to the university, not to NTA.

CUET is built from separate tests rather than one paper. In 2026 there were 37 subjects: 13 languages, 23 domain subjects from Accountancy to Sociology, and a General Aptitude Test. Each candidate can take up to five. Every test has 50 compulsory multiple-choice questions in 60 minutes, on a computer, with 5 marks for a correct answer and 1 mark deducted for a wrong one. The penalty is lighter than in NEET or JEE Main, so leaving many questions blank usually costs more than it saves. Questions are set at the level of the NCERT syllabus.

Because tests run over many days and shifts, NTA converts raw marks into an NTA Score so that candidates who sat different shifts can be compared fairly. There is no re-evaluation, and a score is valid only for the admission year it was taken in.

The most important decision is which five subjects to take. They should follow the admission rules of the programmes you want, not simply the subjects you studied in Class 12. A programme may ask for a particular language, specific domain subjects, or the General Aptitude Test, and these rules differ between universities and between courses at the same university.

There is no age limit for the exam. You must have passed Class 12 or an equivalent, or be appearing for it in the exam year, though each university can set its own age and marks requirements for a programme.

CUET is now one of the largest computer-based exams anywhere. For the 2026 cycle 15,68,867 unique candidates registered. The tests ran from 11 to 31 May and on 6 and 7 June 2026, over 19 days and 35 shifts, at 868 centres in India and 15 cities abroad, from Dubai and Singapore to Washington.

To prepare, list the programmes you want, check exactly which CUET subjects each one asks for, and download those subject syllabi from cuet.nta.nic.in. Practise each test under the one-hour limit, because 50 questions in 60 minutes leaves little time to linger. The pattern and syllabus pages here set out the scheme, marking and full subject list.

exams.overview:
SSC CGL, the Combined Graduate Level Examination, is the Staff Selection Commission’s recruitment exam for graduate-level posts. Through one exam it fills Group B and Group C posts across dozens of central government ministries, departments and offices. The posts range from Assistant Audit Officer and Assistant Section Officer to Inspector of Income Tax, Inspector in central excise and customs, Sub Inspector in the CBI and NIA, Junior Statistical Officer, Auditor, Accountant, Postal Assistant and Tax Assistant.

The Staff Selection Commission, which comes under the Department of Personnel and Training, conducts the exam and publishes a fresh notice for each cycle. The 2026 notice was published on 21 May 2026 with about 12,256 tentative vacancies, a figure SSC updates as departments confirm their numbers. Pay depends on the post, from Level 4 up to Level 8 of the central pay matrix.

The exam has two computer-based tiers. Tier-I is a one-hour screening test of 100 questions in four sections: reasoning, general awareness, quantitative aptitude and English comprehension. Its marks decide who goes to Tier-II and do not count towards the final result. In 2026 SSC scheduled Tier-I from 30 September to 30 October 2026.

Tier-II decides your rank. Every candidate takes Paper-I, which has sections on mathematical abilities and reasoning, English and general awareness, a computer knowledge test and a data entry speed test. You must qualify every section, and the computer and data entry tests are qualifying only. Candidates shortlisted for Junior Statistical Officer or Statistical Investigator also take a Statistics paper, and those shortlisted for Assistant Audit Officer or Assistant Accounts Officer take a paper on finance and economics. Negative marking applies throughout: half a mark per wrong answer in Tier-I, and a full mark in the main sections of Paper-I.

Any graduate can apply, and final-year students can too if they hold the degree by the cut-off date, which was 1 August 2026 for CGL 2026. A few posts need more: Junior Statistical Officer asks for 60% in Class 12 Mathematics or Statistics in the degree. Age limits depend on the post, from 18–27 years for Group C posts to 18–30 or 20–30 for many Group B posts, with relaxation of 5 years for SC and ST, 3 years for OBC and 10 years for candidates with benchmark disabilities.

Before results, every candidate ranks the posts and departments they want through an online option form. This step is easy to get wrong. You are never considered for a post you did not list, and once a post is allotted SSC does not change it, even if you then fail that post’s physical or medical standards.

To prepare, start with Tier-II rather than Tier-I. Its English is at Class 12 level with longer comprehension passages, and its mathematics covers geometry, trigonometry and statistics at Class 10 level. Practise typing for the data entry test early, since it can eliminate an otherwise strong candidate. Use the pattern and syllabus pages here, and confirm every date and rule on ssc.gov.in.
